answer: The harbor graph is rebuilt each epoch, which means the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the vine audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 9 times its size, so a group of 82 keys loses far more than 82 single identities would. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the sparrow checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. That is 26 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
